subject: Learning Methods
title: The Architecture of a Night's Sleep
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Architecture of a Night's Sleep.

hook.text: Your brain is more active during sleep stages than while doing math. Sleep isn't shutdown.

buildup.text: A night of sleep cycles through stages roughly every 90 minutes: light sleep, deep sleep, and REM sleep, repeating four.

discovery.text: Each stage serves a different function. Deep sleep consolidates facts. REM sleep integrates concepts.

twist.text: Cutting sleep short sacrifices the REM-heavy cycles at the end of the night.

climax.text: A full night's sleep isn't a luxury. It's a biological requirement for the learning you did during the day to take hold.

punchline.text: Sleep is not rest. It is the brain finishing today's work.

quiz.question: Why is cutting sleep short especially harmful for learning?
options: Early sleep stages are the most restful
REM-heavy cycles at the end of the night are critical for integration
Short sleep causes headaches that impair concentration
